chunks: From him, from Bunān ibn Muḥammad, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who married a woman but had not consummated with her, then committed zina. What is upon him? He said: “He is to be flogged with the hadd punishment, his head is to be shaved, separation is to be made between him and his family, and he is to be exiled for one year.”

key_terms.وَلَمْ يَدْخُلْ بِهَا: had not consummated the marriage with her
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ الْحَدَّ: he is to receive the prescribed hadd flogging
key_terms.يُحْلَقُ رَأْسُهُ: his head is to be shaved
key_terms.يُفَرَّقُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ أَهْلِهِ: he is to be separated from his family
key_terms.يُنْفَى سَنَةً: he is to be exiled for one year

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a married man who has not consummated marriage and then commits zina?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling concerning a man who has contracted marriage but has not consummated it and then commits zina. It outlines the prescribed hadd and accompanying legal consequences, indicating a specific penal ruling in Shi'i fiqh.
